messages:
maya: Hey team — setting up kubectl on my new M1 Mac. I downloaded the kubeconfig from onboarding but `kubectl get ns` errors with: `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. Any quick checks? I'm on macOS Sonoma, kubectl v1.27 via brew.

devon: Could be a truncated cert in the kubeconfig or your local CA bundle. Quick checks: open `~/.kube/config` and make sure the `certificate-authority-data` block is intact (long base64). Also verify `KUBECONFIG` env var. Try:

```
cat ~/.kube/config | sed -n '1,120p'
kubectl version --client
echo $KUBECONFIG
```

samir: +1. If the kubeconfig has an OIDC or aws sso flow, you'll also need the credential plugin installed. For AWS we usually use `aws-iam-authenticator` or AWS CLI v2 SSO. If the cert is missing entirely, re-download from the onboarding portal: https://onboard.redwood.ai/kubeconfigs — otherwise ping infra to reissue.

ops-bot: Note: If kubeconfig references an internal CA, you may need to point `SSL_CERT_FILE` at a PEM bundle that includes our internal root. See docs: https://internal.redwood.ai/security/ca

lisa: FWIW I hit something like this on M1. macOS/OpenSSL from brew sometimes isn't wired up to the system cert store. I did this and it fixed my local client checks:

```
brew install openssl@3
brew link --force openssl@3
export SSL_CERT_FILE="$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/etc/openssl/cert.pem"
kubectl get ns
```

devon: If you want to inspect the chain directly, run:

```
openssl s_client -showcerts -connect api.redwood.internal:443
```

maya: I re-downloaded the kubeconfig and set `SSL_CERT_FILE` as lisa suggested — `kubectl get ns` now returns the cluster namespaces. Thanks! One follow-up: I get `Forbidden` (403) when trying to `kubectl get pods -n infra-dev`. How do I request access?

lisa: I can grant that. What namespace exactly?

maya: infra-dev (and would like view access to `dev` too eventually).

lisa: Done — granted `view` role in `infra-dev` for 30d, and added you to the request queue for `dev` access. Try:

```
kubectl auth can-i get pods -n infra-dev
```

ops-bot: Permission change applied by lisa at 1769456890.

maya: `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n infra-dev` now returns "yes". Confirmed access. Thanks everyone :tada:
